rounds.proof_sketch: Input shape is fixed at [16, 256, 256] (3D tensor). The mutation is in argmin_kernel_2d which is only invoked when ndim == 2. For 3D inputs, the code takes the 'else if (ndim == 3)' branch and calls argmin_kernel_3d exclusively. The mutated kernel is never executed.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes threadIdx.x to threadIdx.y on line 15 of argmin_kernel_2d. However, with the fixed input specification of shape [16, 256, 256], the input tensor has ndim=3. In the argmin_cuda function, the kernel selection logic checks 'if (ndim == 2)' to invoke the 2D kernel, otherwise 'else if (ndim == 3)' invokes the 3D kernel. Since the input is always 3D, argmin_kernel_2d is never called, and the mutation has zero effect on execution. The argmin_kernel_3d kernel remains unchanged between original and mutant, producing identical results.
rounds.kill_strategy: The mutation is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract because the mutated code path (argmin_kernel_2d) is unreachable with 3D inputs. To kill this mutant would require changing the input shape to 2D, which violates the testing contract.
rounds.recommendations: When designing mutation tests for GPU kernels with multiple dispatch paths (e.g., 2D vs 3D kernels), ensure test inputs cover all paths. This mutant in the 2D kernel went undetected because all tests used 3D inputs. Add separate test configurations with 2D input shapes to exercise both kernel variants.
